scores.concept: ONE ISLAND, ONE TAP — the void's window
scores.notes: STRONG: icons in pips (hero emoji from COPY.heroCue :1543-1664) so a non-reader knows the goal; tap-the-window = voidling.chomp() + audio.pop (void3d.ts:75) doubles as the audio-unlock gesture (audio3d.ts:317-324); pupils follow the orbit (void3d.ts:2340-2347); '.tag' reused as the world chip keeps firstframe.mjs:215-218 selectors alive; pip-hop on return is a real reward loop; LANDMARK HUD as a 'grow until it fills' size bar is the best child-readable HUD of the three. PERF (2/5, my domain): a FULL 360-degree orbit at radius 28 around a void parked ON THE RIM (Maple stage = waterfall lip, 3D (190,207.5), island.ts:278) means half of every 90 s turn looks inland across the whole plateau; three.js culls by frustum not occlusion and camera.far is 1000 (prototype3d.ts:663) so nothing on a 600-unit island is ever culled — the inland half of the orbit is the 4,694-call class (:10496-10500), not the 1,241 class the concept budgets ('draw calls at each authored MENU_STAGE <= 1,400' is measured at one azimuth, the bar is silent on the other 180 degrees). Shadows forced off on EVERY rung via the intro toggle with the first-toggle recompile stall (docs/AUDIT-2026-08-23.md:316) left as 'measure whether'; no menu-side degrade — if the iPhone 11 misses 16.7 ms the only lever is a re-plan. USABILITY (3): no fail-forward inside a world by default (a six-year-old who cannot reach the Town Hall at ~132 s (:1517-1520) sits on pip 3 forever while pips 4-5 stay padlocked; only the finish rule opens the NEXT world), BY MYSELF buried in #settings, 'LEVEL 7 OF 30' text on the home screen (Hole.io keeps that on the end card). FLOW (3): CONTINUE returns to the menu so chaining levels is 2 taps (CONTINUE, PLAY) plus a hard cut into the descent each time; menu re-entry warps the void to a stage (:2262-2270 pattern) — a visible teleport unless the end card's blur hides it, unaddressed. BUILD (3): six authored MENU_STAGE rows + warp there/back + the orbit rework it will need after the first draw-call series lands. OWNER (4): every 2026-09-06 decision honoured, but keeps Hole.io's exact tab hues and #4c3cbe on HOME, and the caption-on-menu is against 'kept it simple'.

scores.concept: Splash Alive — the living island menu with the five-bite ladder
scores.notes: STRONG: the cheapest frame of the three — 22-unit camera, height 9, ±6 degree pendulum over 16 s (peak 0.04 deg/frame), crowdGate 138 units (:10277), shadows left as the renderer has them at rungs 0-1 (no first-toggle recompile on the menu), DPR 1.3, bloom off; fail-forward after 3 misses with the skipped pip left open; 'NOT YET!' + coins still paid + the honest frozen counter; EAT bar holds its high-water mark while the number stays honest (playerScore can fall at :2945); PLAY 88 px; BY MYSELF visible on the goal line; per-level camera nudge (L3 toward the hero, L4 the family visible behind the void) is the best 'the diorama shows the goal' idea on the table; CONTINUE chains straight into the next pip via resetMatch (:7695) — 1 tap per level. WEAK — identity (3): 'borrow the measured skeleton exactly' means Hole.io's own #4c3cbe ground over 45% and its blue/violet/orange tabs; the creature saves it from a hole but the screen is a palette-swap away from the reference. First-second (3): the logo floats over a MOVING sky inside the window plus a world plate, a season chip, a text goal line and a BY MYSELF chip — busier than the other two, and the goal line is prose for a non-reader. PERF (3): honest ratio bar (<=1.15) and the 1.3x draw-call bar against in-match r=12, but 0.5 crew-days for six worlds x two rungs x moverStats is under-budgeted, there is no menu-side degrade if the 22-unit wedge still measures hot on Lantern's ~966 walkers (life.ts:6813), the camera at height 9 puts pedestrians and the void's own body across the near plane, and the pendulum direction (which way the wedge faces) is unspecified — direction, not distance, decides draw calls on this island. BUILD (4): smallest scope, but it smuggles in unasked work (season lights a lantern emissive, newsroom headline moves to the end card). OWNER (4): all five goals, board retired, first touch, one tap; 'exactly Hole.io' is the opposite of 'we improve'.

scores.concept: LIVING SPLASH — the key art rendered live, five pips under it, one tap to play
scores.notes: STRONG: the only concept that reads 'making our splash image alive' literally — a feathered oval mask over our own #33175e->#0d0821 cosmos (index.html:888-896 stays) makes the island FLOAT, the creature sits below at real scale looking UP at the landmark (the key art's stack, minus the poster mouth), teal/violet/plum tabs, no borrowed hex anywhere. PERF (4, the deciding criterion for me): the only plan with a menu-side adapter decoupled from qLevel (3-step menuRung on measured dtRaw >20 ms: DPR 1.0 -> shadows off via the intro toggle :10505-10509 -> frozen orbit at 30 fps with island.update dt doubled so water keeps its speed) so an iPhone 11 that misses the bar degrades itself instead of forcing a re-plan, while qa/ladder.mjs's MENU GATE (:106-114) stays green because __quality() never moves; azimuth a0 chosen per world so the pendulum (±12 deg / 24 s, 0.24 px/frame) never sweeps the far plateau — the only concept that treats DIRECTION as the draw-call variable; renderer.compile() pre-warm for the shadowless program set; visibility gate plus 60 s / 5 min idle tiers; refreshHud on the freeze list (the others forgot it, :10810); device bar read through __menuState on the daughter's phone via the Capacitor shell, not the sandbox. Why not 5: 58 units at height 24 is the WIDEST framing of the three (more in frustum than 22 or 28), the 900 ms post-HOME camera ease is an unbudgeted swoop through expensive azimuths, the 20 ms degrade threshold tolerates a 50 fps menu on a 60 Hz panel, and 'compile after the first frame' lands a stall right after the boot cover drops (:10931-10935). USABILITY (3): 36/46 px pips are under the 44 px finger target, pips carry NUMERALS so a non-reader depends on the text goal line, the creature chomps on a 14 s timer but a tap on him does nothing (no first-second interaction), PLAY is the smallest of the three at 64 px. Fail-forward with 'YOU CAN SKIP AHEAD', the 'stolen' LANDMARK result and heroProp excluded from rival bites (:10770-10774) are right. FLOW (4): CONTINUE -> next pip without a reload, TRY AGAIN, HOME with an ease; first-session autoplay (:6559-6562) called out. BUILD (4): 16.5 days is the honest number and S0 puts throw-if-absent guards on pickerfit.mjs:245-260 and firstframe.mjs:220 BEFORE the menu changes — the governor's rule 4 done first; BOOK re-parenting of #trophies/#topvoids and the #daily condition rewrite (:7967) are the two moderate-risk items. OWNER (5): every decision honoured, measure-first with guards, 'LEVEL n OF 30' kept off the menu as Hole.io does, and it improves rather than copies.

winner: LIVING SPLASH — the key art rendered live, five pips under it, one tap to play (29 vs 25 vs 23). It wins on the two criteria I own: it is the only plan that can miss 16.7 ms on an iPhone 11 and still ship (menu-only degrade ladder independent of qLevel, direction-controlled pendulum, pre-warmed shadow toggle, throw-if-absent probe guards landed before the mask is cut), and it is the only one that improves the splash rather than palette-swapping Hole.io.
grafts_from_runners_up: From ONE ISLAND: a tap on the void (or anywhere in the window) = voidling.chomp() + audio.pop() through the rig API (void3d.ts:75) — it is the first-second delight AND the audio-unlock gesture (audio3d.ts:317-324); drop LIVING SPLASH's 14 s chomp timer to a fallback when nobody taps.
From ONE ISLAND: pupils track the camera azimuth (lookX/lookY, void3d.ts:2340-2347) so he watches the child; keep LIVING SPLASH's gaze-up beat as the secondary cue.

From ONE ISLAND: goal ICONS inside the pips (burger / basket / the world's hero emoji from COPY.heroCue :1543-1664 / crown / globe) instead of numerals, and 44 px pips with a 57 px current (1.29x, recon.md:29) — a six-year-old cannot read '3' as 'eat the town hall' and cannot hit 36 px reliably.
From ONE ISLAND: LANDMARK HUD as a size bar R / (heroProp.radius / EAT_RATIO) that reads 'grow until it fills' (:6114-6116, :3673) — replace LIVING SPLASH's 'you 3.2 / need 5.9' numbers.

From ONE ISLAND: the pip-hop on menu re-entry (finished pip flips grey/magenta 180 ms, green ring hops right 220 ms with audio.ready()) — play it on HOME after a win even though CONTINUE chains directly.
From ONE ISLAND: never audio.lose() on a failed goal level (audio.ready() instead) — LIVING SPLASH says 'no punishment' but does not name the sting.

From Splash Alive: make the 22-unit / height-9 close wedge the DEFAULT stage and open out toward 58 units only where the S0 draw-call series says the world can afford it; 58 is the widest of the three framings and direction control alone will not save Lantern or Game Day (6,537 edibles, :7379).

From Splash Alive: the per-level camera nudge — L3 slides the target 30% toward the hero, L4 shows the family standing frozen behind the void (rivals.update frozen :10290, but visible) so 'BE THE BIGGEST VOID' has a picture; LIVING SPLASH removes the family from the diorama entirely.
From Splash Alive: the EAT bar holds its high-water mark while the number stays honest (playerScore drops on a hunter steal, :2945) — a bar that retreats reads as a bug to a child.
From Splash Alive: PLAY at 88 px tall (LIVING SPLASH's 64 px is the smallest of the three; the reference is full-width and fat) and 'NOT YET!' as the miss headline instead of 'TIME'S UP'.
From Splash Alive: the scared blink on a locked-pip tap (setMood via the rig API) alongside LIVING SPLASH's 6 px shake and 'FINISH LEVEL 2 FIRST' line.
what_all_three_missed: Direction, not distance, is the draw-call variable and none of them budget it as a series: three.js culls by frustum only, camera.far is 1000 (prototype3d.ts:663, raised to 1400 at :10492) so nothing on a ~600-unit island is ever far-culled; the S0/menuframe probe must sample renderer.info across the FULL azimuth range the orbit/pendulum will visit (and the 900 ms post-HOME ease in LIVING SPLASH), not one parked frame.

The PLAY hand-off double-flips shadows and reallocates render targets on the one frame that matters: every concept restores shadows/DPR/bloom on leaving the menu, then the intro turns shadows off again at :10505-10509 and restores at introT<=0; and bloom's composer calls setPixelRatio/setSize every frame (:10948-10950) so the first bloom frame after a DPR change reallocates the mip chain — the hitch lands on the tap. Cheapest fix: leave the menu's shadow state in place across PLAY and let the intro's own restore bring it back; restore DPR/bloom during the intro, not on the tap.

Reduced motion: index.html:1861 already has a prefers-reduced-motion block and the app is rated 4+; no concept says what the orbit, the PLAY breathe or the pip pulse do under it (freeze the orbit, kill the pulses) — Apple review and epileptic/vestibular children both care.

document.hidden already pauses a running match (prototype3d.ts:7750-7751); every concept adds a second visibilitychange gate on the rAF without saying how the two interact (a hidden menu that resumes into a paused match, or an end card under a paused rAF).

-webkit-mask-image: two concepts cut the window with CSS mask-image; iOS WebKit in the Capacitor shell still needs the -webkit- prefix and mask-image on a position:fixed layer over a WebGL canvas promotes #menu to its own compositor layer at DPR 2 — cheap, but unmeasured, and on iOS the mask feather must be a raster gradient, not an SVG mask, or it re-rasterises per frame.

Growth is pace-coupled to score (pace = playerScore / par, :9725): a SET level that sends a child hunting eight cars and five houses scores low, grows slow and never reaches the finale surge — the SET table and the LANDMARK reachability are one measurement, not two; nobody runs qa/pace.mjs under a SET-style eating pattern.

The owner reads numbers and nobody gives him the funnel: no concept adds track('level_start'/'level_win'/'level_fail', {world, goal, secs, attempt}) beside the existing track() calls (:7774 match_quit, :8216 save_migrated), so after launch there is no per-pip clear rate to tune EAT=0.6*par or the fail-forward threshold against — the polish plan's 'median tester clears level 1 in one run' bar is unmeasurable as planned.

The end card at 430x932 already overflows (index.html:2263-2269) and all three ADD #endPips, a level bar and a locked-island illustration while keeping #endStats, #drop and the sticker finds — no height budget, no scroll decision, no probe (qa/endfit2 exists and none names it).

Memory, not just ms: bloom's composer targets stay allocated when bloomOn=false, the menu's DPR change plus shadow map plus the 2.2 MB menu.mp3 re-decode on every HOME (audio3d.ts:3931 releaseBuf) all live in a Capacitor WKWebView with a jetsam limit; none of the three names a heap bar for the menu state on the reference phone.

What a rival does in the diorama's frozen family: freezing rivals.update while onMenu leaves the family mid-pose (mouth open, trail sprite) wherever the last match ended on the post-HOME menu; nobody says the family is re-posed or hidden before the camera eases in.

Menu input plumbing: the window band is transparent but #menu still owns pointer events; a tap-chomp on the canvas needs #menu to forward the tap, and the match's pointerdown handler (:3397 startMatch, guarded on armed) plus lastInput (attract mode :9849) must not see it — none of the three specifies where the tap is caught.

The first-session path (no voidPlayed, :6559-6562) skips the menu entirely and autoplays Maple level 1; only LIVING SPLASH notes it and none says what the daughter sees on session 2 when the ladder, the fail-forward and the pip row appear for the first time — no tutorial beat for the pips themselves, on a screen whose whole point is those five circles.
